parcalar.metin: [excited] From Greece to Mexico, from India to Morocco... millions believe this! [whispers] One look... can make you sick.
[dramatic] But the real shock... [pause] this fear is five thousand years old!
[curious] Clay tablets from Ugarit, in Syria, already warned about the evil eye. It began in Mesopotamia... then spread to Egypt, Greece and Rome.

[serious] The Greek philosopher Plutarch said: the eye... shoots rays! [amused] The Romans hung a strange charm on their doors. Its shape? [whispers] Let's not say... it's carved in stone at Leptis Magna!
[dramatic] Centuries later, Rome had a pope: Pius the Ninth. Everyone he blessed... met disaster! [whispers] People called him cursed... and threw his medals out the window.

[curious] And the blue bead? One hundred thirty years ago, Arab glassmakers arrived in Izmir. Their smoke choked the city... they were pushed out! They settled in the village of Görece. [excited] They melted broken bottles... into eyes!
[sad] Today that village is called Nazarköy. Most furnaces have gone cold.
[curious] So why won't this belief die? An economist studied one hundred eighty-six societies. [dramatic] The answer is one word: envy! More inequality... more evil eye!
[excited] Same eyes... same fear! Full story on the channel.
